blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reference-frame stabilization registers every frame of a hovering-drone video onto one reference frame, keeping object positions comparable. The registration pipelines it relies on are selected on feature-matching benchmarks in which only the camera moves. Over a busy intersection, vehicles moving together supply mutually consistent correspondences that can draw the robust homography estimate toward their motion: consensus capture, which inlier statistics cannot flag. A two-part benchmark measures it and the object masking meant to prevent it. A static protocol scores ten pipelines under exactly known homographies on 4K aerial frames, tuned on a site-disjoint split at a matched resolution and feature budget. A dynamic protocol scores them at an offline and a real-time budget on hovers selected from the video alone to span the amount and coherence of moving foreground, plus a stationary control. It measures background alignment, object position error and the share of a moving group's displacement an estimate follows, against a pseudo-ground-truth reference audited with manually annotated ground control points, which also score every candidate. On static scenes, tuned AKAZE, RootSIFT, SIFT and BRISK lead, retuning the matcher thresholds raises the mean average accuracy (mAA) by at most 0.0062, and masking costs less than 0.005. Unmasked ORB is captured on 28 of 304 real-time dynamic pairs and on 6 offline; its real-time captured estimates have a median corner error of 18.8 px yet typical inlier counts and ratios. Masking removes capture for every pipeline and leaves the leading pipelines unchanged. Code, data and results are released.
blocks.zh: 参照框架稳定记录了每个悬浮式视频的帧到一个参照框架,使物体位置具有可比性。 它所依赖的注册管道是根据只有相机移动的特征匹配基准选择的. 在繁忙的交叉路口上,车辆一起移动,提供相互一致的通信,可以引领强烈的图谱学估计走向他们的动作:协商一致的捕捉,而更强烈的统计不能标榜这一点。 由两部分组成的基准衡量它和物体遮盖是为了防止它。 静态协议在4K空中架设的完全已知的同位素下对10条管道进行评分,根据匹配的分辨率和特征预算,以一个站点-分离的分割进行调制. 动态协议在离线时给它们评分,而实时预算则只从视频中选择盘旋,以覆盖移动前景的数量和一致性,再加上固定控制. 它对照经过人工注释的地面控制点审计的伪地面真实参考,衡量背景调整、对象位置错误和移动组移位的比例。 在静态场景中,调制了AKAZE,RootSIFT,SIFT和BRISK的铅,重新调整了匹配器阈值,将平均平均精度(mAA)提升了最多0.062,遮掩成本低于0.005. 304个实时动态对中的28个和6个离线捕获未装模作样的ORB;其实时捕获的估计数中位角误差为18.8 px,但典型的更强计数和比值. 面具可以清除每条管道的捕获量,使主要管道保持不变。 代码,数据和结果发布.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Reference-frame stabilization is the registration model used when object positions must stay
consistent over a long hover, during which wind keeps shifting and rotating the view: every frame is aligned directly onto one
fixed reference frame, so that error does not accumulate and a position measured in frame k k is
comparable with one measured minutes earlier. Trajectory extraction from high-altitude UAV ( UAV ) video is the application studied here, and traffic monitoring supplies the footage, but
the requirement is shared by any analysis that compares moving objects across time in image or map
coordinates, such as river surface velocimetry ( Ljubičić et al., 2021a ) . The estimate is a homography, and the pipeline that produces it (feature detector,
descriptor, matcher, robust estimator, and, where objects are annotated, a masking strategy that
withholds them from feature detection) is assembled from components each of which has been
benchmarked extensively ( Jin et al., 2021a ; Efe et al., 2021a ; Barath et al., 2023a ) .

blocks.en:
Those benchmarks evaluate correspondence accuracy on scenes without independently moving content:
planar surfaces, landmark facades, building walls. The only source of disagreement between their
two views is the camera. A hovering drone over a busy intersection presents the opposite case. The
camera barely moves, and dozens of objects in the frame move without it, many of them together: a
platoon released by a green light translates as a unit, and every vehicle in it supplies
correspondences that agree with one another under a single transform, the one describing their
motion. If those correspondences win the consensus, the robust estimator does not fail. It solves
the problem it was posed, returning a homography that is internally consistent and well supported
but describes the vehicles rather than the road ( Fig. 1 ).

blocks.en:
We call this failure consensus capture , and it has a consequence for evaluation before it
has one for method design. Inlier count, inlier ratio, and reprojection error measure the
self-consistency of a fit, and a coherently moving foreground is self-consistent by construction.
Where it wins, these quantities are no longer merely weak proxies for accuracy, as they are already
known to be on static scenes ( Jin et al., 2021a ; Barath et al., 2023a ) ; they become
anti-informative, because the moving-object consensus can be the cleaner of the two available
fits. An evaluation that reads them cannot detect capture. What is needed scores the alignment of
the static world directly, makes a moving-object consensus observable, and relates it to how much
of the frame moves and how coherently. To our knowledge no matching or registration benchmark provides
this: none combines
independently moving content with reference geometry ( Section 2 ), so a risk flagged for
airborne video ( Kirchhof & Stilla, 2006a ) has gone unmeasured.

blocks.en:
Capture matters most where trajectories are used one at a time. Macroscopic quantities such as flow
and density average a transient offset away, but microscopic analyses read individual trajectories
and their derivatives: car following, lane changes ( Kim et al., 2026a ) , per-vehicle noise
emission ( Espadaler-Clapés et al., 2023a ) , and surrogate safety measures such as
time-to-collision, post-encroachment time and the deceleration rate to avoid a
crash ( Abdel-Aty et al., 2023a ; Espadaler-Clapés et al., 2025a ) , which drone trajectory
datasets now provide or are built to support ( Zheng et al., 2024a ; Fonod et al., 2025b ) .
Under reference-frame registration each frame is registered on its own, so nothing ties a captured estimate to those of neighboring frames: its error
follows the group’s motion and is present only while the group holds the consensus. Speeds and
accelerations are differences of positions over fractions of a second, so an error that varies from
frame to frame in this way is amplified in them ( Punzo et al., 2011a ) . The accuracy these
datasets aim for is correspondingly tight: the inD dataset requires a positioning error below 0.1 m 0.1\text{\,}\mathrm{m} ( Bock et al., 2020a ) , under two pixels at the GSD ( GSD ) of the footage studied here
( Section 3 ), whereas the captured estimates of Section 7.3 have a median
corner error of 18.8 px 18.8\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} , about a meter on the ground, against the reference estimator. Since
the estimates pulled toward the group keep typical inlier statistics, a pipeline captured on a few
frames passes their error, unflagged, to every trajectory in those frames. Several of these datasets are also recorded lower
than the 140 m to 150 m 140\text{\,}\mathrm{m}150\text{\,}\mathrm{m} studied here: inD from up to 100 m 100\text{\,}\mathrm{m} at about 4 cm 4\text{\,}\mathrm{cm} per pixel ( Bock et al., 2020a ) and the intersections of CitySim from 120 m 120\text{\,}\mathrm{m} ( Zheng et al., 2024a ) ; a view that covers less ground can give a vehicle group
of the same size a larger share of the frame and of its features.

blocks.en:
We provide such an evaluation in two parts. Part I is a static protocol under exactly known
homographies and photometric degradation, on 4K frames from a multi-drone experiment over Songdo,
South Korea: one from each of the 29 29 viewpoints from which its ten drones recorded 20 20 intersections. It establishes what each pipeline can do when nothing moves and which of its
settings matter, extending the campaign of Fonod et al. (2025b) with paired trials,
per-pipeline tuning on a site-disjoint split, and a matched resolution and feature budget. Part II is a dynamic
protocol on nine hovers over busy intersections, each registered onto a reference frame selected
from the video alone to span the amount and coherence of
moving foreground, plus a stationary control that separates the removal of moving objects from the removal
of texture. It runs every pipeline at an offline and a real-time point of Part I’s budget grid.
Real footage has no true homography, so Part II measures background alignment outside the annotated
objects, the position error a trajectory inherits, the direction of the error relative to the
dominant motion, and the share of a moving group’s displacement an estimate follows, which
measures capture where it happens. Its pseudo-ground-truth reference estimator is audited against
manually annotated GCP (image positions of static ground points, not surveyed coordinates),
which also score every candidate directly, so that the
masking comparison does not depend on the reference estimator’s own masking. Masking with HBB and OBB is a controlled axis throughout, since the shape of a mask could
matter in either direction ( Section 5 ).

blocks.en:
On hovers over Songdo intersections, the measurement finds capture. At the real-time budget,
unmasked ORB is captured in all five cases that present a coherently moving group, the four with
much moving foreground and the stationary control, on 28 28 of the 304 304 pairs that carry
one, though 22 22 of them in a single case. The 17 17 within the first second are pulls toward
the group; 10 10 of the 11 11 beyond it are breakdowns of the estimate, which unmasked ORB also
shows with no group in view. At the offline budget capture is rarer (unmasked ORB, 6 6 pairs in
two cases). Estimates pulled toward a group cannot be told apart by their inlier statistics: their
inlier counts and ratios match those of the same pipeline at the nearest offsets of the same case,
at both budgets. Masking removes capture for every pipeline at both budgets while leaving
the leading pipelines, SIFT, RootSIFT and AKAZE, where they were; for real-time ORB, whose feature
budget it also returns to the ground, the captured pairs can account for at most a quarter of the gain. HBB and OBB do not differ at these densities and orientations, where the two geometries
withhold nearly the same pixels.
Averaged over all nine cases, four of which never present a moving group, the masking benefit is
either not significant or smaller than the repeatability of the GCP ( Section 7.5 ). The conclusions are bounded by the
moving share of these cases; the protocol is not, and it applies unchanged to footage from lower
altitude or over denser traffic, where that share is larger.

blocks.en: 1.1 Contributions
blocks.zh: 1.1 缴款

blocks.en:
1. A benchmark for the complete registration pipeline of reference-based UAV stabilization in
dynamic urban scenes: a static protocol under exactly known homographies
( Section 6 ) and a dynamic protocol on real hovering-drone footage at an offline and a
real-time compute budget ( Section 7 ). It covers the pipelines a deployed
stabilization library exposes, as a measurement of that system rather than a leaderboard
of state-of-the-art matchers ( Section 3.2 ). 2. An evaluation methodology for dynamic scenes, where self-consistency statistics are
unreliable: background-alignment measures that need no ground-truth homography,
object-level errors that bound the position error a trajectory inherits, two measures that
make consensus capture observable (the direction of the error and the share of a moving
group’s displacement an estimate follows), and a GCP audit that measures the error of the
pseudo-ground truth and supplies an independent comparison ( Section 4 ), under a
pre-specified analysis plan ( Section 4.9 ). 3. A case-selection procedure that measures from the video alone how much of the foreground
moves, how coherently, and when, and chooses the cases and their reference frames to span
these conditions, under which capture can arise; its
measurements are validated against published vehicle trajectories
( Section 7.1 ). 4. A measurement of consensus capture and of object-aware masking on real footage: at the
real-time budget unmasked ORB is captured in every case that presents a coherent group, its
pull toward the group is invisible to inlier statistics, and capture disappears under
masking at detection ( Sections 7.3 and 7.5 ). 5. The public release of the benchmark implementation ( Fonod, 2026f ) and of its
data ( Fonod & Geroliminis, 2026b ) (annotated frames, cases, GCP and every
campaign’s results), from which every benchmark number is regenerated by a command. Also
released are hbb2obb ( Fonod, 2026e ) , the SAM-assisted conversion of HBB to OBB that makes OBB masks available at benchmark scale, and Songdo
Vision OBB ( Fonod & Geroliminis, 2026c ) , the OBB version of Songdo
Vision ( Fonod et al., 2026a ) , together with the human-verified oriented reference against
which the conversion is validated ( Sections 5.1 and E ).

blocks.en:
A benchmark for the complete registration pipeline of reference-based UAV stabilization in
dynamic urban scenes: a static protocol under exactly known homographies
( Section 6 ) and a dynamic protocol on real hovering-drone footage at an offline and a
real-time compute budget ( Section 7 ). It covers the pipelines a deployed
stabilization library exposes, as a measurement of that system rather than a leaderboard
of state-of-the-art matchers ( Section 3.2 ).

An evaluation methodology for dynamic scenes, where self-consistency statistics are
unreliable: background-alignment measures that need no ground-truth homography,
object-level errors that bound the position error a trajectory inherits, two measures that
make consensus capture observable (the direction of the error and the share of a moving
group’s displacement an estimate follows), and a GCP audit that measures the error of the
pseudo-ground truth and supplies an independent comparison ( Section 4 ), under a
pre-specified analysis plan ( Section 4.9 ).

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Correspondence estimation has been surveyed repeatedly as it moved from hand-crafted operators to
learned ones ( Ma et al., 2021a ) . The pipelines
benchmarked here span three generations of that work. Hand-crafted detectors and descriptors, from
SIFT ( Lowe, 2004a ) and its RootSIFT normalization ( Arandjelović & Zisserman, 2012a ) to the
binary ORB ( Rublee et al., 2011a ) and BRISK ( Leutenegger et al., 2011a ) and the nonlinear
scale spaces of KAZE ( Alcantarilla et al., 2012a ) and AKAZE ( Alcantarilla et al., 2013a ) , remain
the default in deployed stabilization pipelines, because they need no training data, no
accelerator, and no assumption about the imagery. Learned detectors and descriptors replace one or
both stages with a network trained for repeatability and matchability, among them
SuperPoint ( DeTone et al., 2018a ) , DISK ( Tyszkiewicz et al., 2020a ) ,
DeDoDe ( Edstedt et al., 2024b ) , Key.Net ( Barroso-Laguna et al., 2019a ) and
XFeat ( Potje et al., 2024a ) ; learned matchers such as LightGlue ( Lindenberger et al., 2023a ) replace the nearest-neighbor search and its ratio test with attention over the two keypoint sets;
and detector-free methods such as LoFTR ( Sun et al., 2021a ) drop keypoints and match dense features
directly. Dense matchers such as RoMa ( Edstedt et al., 2024c ) go further and estimate a warp and
its certainty for every pixel, from which correspondences are sampled.
A stabilization pipeline is chosen as a whole and its components interact (a matcher accepts only
certain descriptors, a detector-free method has no keypoint budget), so the comparison of Section 6.2 spans all three. Two properties of this literature shape the protocol.
Orientation estimation is not universal, so several learned models are effectively upright, which
is why rotation is swept, as Tareen & Saleem (2018a) sweep it for the classical detectors,
which they find unequally invariant to it; and the input resolution of
a learned model is a memory bound rather than a free choice, which is why the compute budget is an
axis of the benchmark.

A parallel line of work regresses the transform from an image
pair ( DeTone et al., 2016a ) . Zhang et al. (2020a) observe that a loss computed uniformly
over the image cannot keep moving or non-planar objects from contributing to it, and learn a
content mask that rejects those regions: the problem measured here, approached by learning what to
ignore instead of by annotating it. These methods lie outside the feature-based family deployed in the trajectory extraction systems of Section 2 .

blocks.en:
RANSAC ( Fischler & Bolles, 1981a ) and its modern variants ( Barath et al., 2020a ; Barath & Matas, 2018a ) make a homography recoverable from contaminated correspondences. That a coherent structure of
outliers can capture the consensus is known ( Stewart, 1997a ) , and Chum et al. (2005a) detect a dominant plane inside the estimator; Section 4.1 explains why that defense
does not transfer to a coherently moving group. Filters that prune matches before the estimator rest
on a similar vote: Jiang & Jiang (2018a) keep matches whose motion agrees in direction and
length, Zhou et al. (2024a) build local motion consensus into a learned matcher, and the motions
of a coherently moving group agree as well.

blocks.en:
Multi-model fitting accepts that a scene may contain several coherent structures and recovers them
jointly, by clustering correspondences ( Toldo & Fusiello, 2008a ; Wong et al., 2011a ) or by fitting
instances progressively inside the robust estimator ( Barath & Matas, 2019a ) .
Vehicles crossing an intersection are such a
second structure, and AdelaideRMF ( Wong et al., 2011a ) does contain independently moving
content. These methods are evaluated by how well correspondences are partitioned among structures,
not by the accuracy of one recovered transform, and AdelaideRMF supplies no reference homography for
the background. Recovering several homographies also leaves open which one describes the ground,
which correspondence counts cannot decide when the moving structure is the larger. Multi-model
fitting is a remedy that changes the estimator; what is missing first is a measurement of the
failure under the estimators actually deployed.

blocks.en:
Comparative studies of classical detectors and descriptors ( Tareen & Saleem, 2018a ) and
HPatches ( Balntas et al., 2017a ) established the vocabulary this field still uses, and Schonberger et al. (2017a) set the pattern of judging hand-crafted and learned features on a
common downstream task. Three benchmarks set the
methodological standard we adopt. Jin et al. (2021a) argue that local features must be judged by
a downstream task rather than by intermediate proxies, and show that carefully tuned classical
pipelines remain competitive with learned ones, a conclusion Efe et al. (2021a) reach on HPatches
by optimizing a single parameter; Barath et al. (2023a) contribute a large-scale homography
benchmark with an explicit tuning-and-test protocol. Their shared lesson is that a comparison is
only as meaningful as the care taken to place every method on equal footing
( Section 4.7 ). None of them measures registration accuracy on a scene whose content
moves independently of the camera ( Table 1 ), because their reference geometry, SfM ( SfM ) or manually labeled correspondences on static structure, must exclude independently moving
objects to work at all. Registration benchmarks that do model change place it between
acquisitions ( Sun et al., 2025a ) . Pseudo-ground truth has a further cost: Brachmann et al. (2021a) show
that the algorithm generating it can reorder the methods evaluated against it, which is why the
reference estimator of Part II is audited against GCP ( Section 4.8 ).

blocks.en:
Excluding independently moving content before a geometric model is fitted is established practice
in dynamic SLAM ( SLAM ). DynaSLAM ( Bescos et al., 2018a ) and DS-SLAM ( Yu et al., 2018a ) segment
likely-moving classes and withhold those regions from tracking and mapping. Both report that suppression keeps
the estimate usable in populated scenes; what is missing is a measurement. Those systems are
evaluated end to end, by trajectory error on indoor sequences with a handful of walking people or
on driving sequences, which does not say how much of the frame the objects may cover before the consensus shifts to them, which box
geometry is worth its cost, or what the failure looks like without suppression. A hovering drone
over an intersection is the opposite regime: a nearly static camera and dozens of vehicles moving
in coherent streams. Isolating the effect needs the masking strategy varied as a controlled axis
while everything else is held fixed ( Section 7.5 ), and a metric that does not read
the objects themselves ( Section 4.3 ).

blocks.en:
Stabilization also names work whose goal is a pleasant camera path rather than a fixed frame of
reference: smoothing the path under geometric constraints ( Grundmann et al., 2011a ) , over a mesh of
local homographies ( Liu et al., 2013a ) , or by learning the warp ( Yu & Ramamoorthi, 2020a ) . Its
measures (cropping ratio,
distortion, a frequency-domain stability score) follow from a perceptual objective, and none asks
where a pixel actually is. A smoothed path may drift from any particular frame, which is
inadmissible when object positions are compared across a recording, and a mesh of local warps can
absorb independent object motion instead of rejecting it. Moving objects enter this literature as a
threat to the global motion estimate, met by adaptive RANSAC ( Choi et al., 2009a ) , clustered motion
vectors ( Wu et al., 2021a ) or foreground trajectories ( Zhao & Ling, 2019a ) , and scored by the
similarity of the output frames, not against reference geometry.

blocks.en:
Registering airborne video to a fixed reference is long established in
photogrammetry ( Kumar et al., 2001a ) . The remote sensing literature on image registration
concentrates on matching across modalities, sensors and acquisition times ( Geng et al., 2025a ) ,
with structural or phase-congruency descriptors built to be insensitive to radiometric
change ( Ye et al., 2017a ; Li et al., 2020a ) and networks trained on large multimodal
datasets ( Wu et al., 2026a ) , so transient content is a nuisance to be removed rather than a
property to be measured.

(Ye等人,2017年a;Li等人,2020年a)和接受大型多式联运培训的网络
数据集(Wu等,2026a),所以瞬间内容是一种需要去除而非被去除的烦恼.

blocks.en:
Vehicle measurement from the air rests on this
registration ( Reinartz et al., 2006a ; Karimi et al., 2006a ) , and moving traffic is a recognized
hazard to it. Kirchhof & Stilla (2006a) warn that many objects moving in the same direction, as on
dense roads, can survive RANSAC and bias the homography, and exclude points at detected motion. Karimi & Lindenbergh (2014a) rule out direct SIFT with RANSAC against the first image of a
helicopter sequence, in part because of the moving vehicles, and chain consecutive homographies
instead. Ljubičić et al. (2021a) compare seven stabilization tools on UAV river footage,
where the water moves and the banks do not, by residual motion at static features. None of these
measures capture or what it costs in position.

blocks.en:
Aerial object detection has well-established
benchmarks ( Ding et al., 2022a ; Zhu et al., 2022a ) , DOTA made OBB standard for
aerial objects, and UAVid ( Lyu et al., 2020a ) separates moving from static cars in 4K UAV video
for semantic segmentation. They evaluate recognition , not the registration that must precede
any use of object positions when the camera moves. Drone-based trajectory datasets show the dependency most
clearly: pNEUMA ( Barmpounakis & Geroliminis, 2020a ) , inD ( Bock et al., 2020a ) ,

The work closest to this paper is Fonod et al. (2025b) , which extracts georeferenced vehicle
trajectories from hovering-drone recordings of urban intersections and stabilizes each frame onto a
reference frame with an object-masked homography, releasing that stage as stabilo ( Fonod, 2026g ) and its parameter study as stabilo-optimize . The vehicles are masked to keep

blocks.en: 3 Problem setting

blocks.en:
Recordings come from hovering drones at approximately constant altitude
( 140 m to 150 m 140\text{\,}\mathrm{m}150\text{\,}\mathrm{m} ) in BEV ( BEV ) at 4K resolution ( 3840 × 2160 3840\times 2160 ), so inter-frame
motion is small and wind-induced. The GSD ( GSD ) is about 5.5 cm 5.5\text{\,}\mathrm{cm} per pixel: the
scale of the homographies that register hovers of this experiment onto its georeferenced
orthophoto ( Fonod et al., 2025b ) ranges from 0.0548 0.0548 to 0.0564 m 0.0564\text{\,}\mathrm{m} per pixel over
eleven hovers. A pixel of registration error is thus about 5.5 cm 5.5\text{\,}\mathrm{cm} on the ground,
and the 5 px 5\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} upper limit of the accuracy interval below is about 28 cm 28\text{\,}\mathrm{cm} .
Every pixel quantity in this paper converts at that rate.
The stabilization model is a reference-frame homography, which holds the static scene in place
over a hover exactly only where that scene is planar. Above-ground structures (buildings, poles,
vegetation) depart from the plane in proportion to how far the platform translates; a hovering
platform translates little but does drift, so the evaluation excludes buildings and large tree
canopy, the largest such structures, by polygons drawn on each reference frame ( Section 4.3 ) and scores
the rest of the static scene. The deployed regime is a
hovering platform, so the geometric perturbation a pipeline has to recover in practice is a few
pixels of drift and a fraction of a degree of yaw per frame relative to the reference, growing
slowly over a recording. Part I samples a wider regime than that, so that a
pipeline’s operating limits are measured, and Section 6 states where the two regimes differ.

blocks.en:
The order is: detection or segmentation → \rightarrow mask construction → \rightarrow feature
detection → \rightarrow description → \rightarrow matching → \rightarrow robust estimation. No
keypoint inside a mask reaches matching, so metrics defined on “removed features” or on a
“dynamic inlier ratio” are not applicable here, and are not used. Where the mask enters the
detector differs between implementations, and it decides what masking can do under a feature
budget; every detector is used with the masking its implementation provides, unmodified. ORB,
BRISK and AKAZE detect outside the mask and then keep their strongest responses up to the budget,
so the keypoints a mask removes are replaced by others. SIFT, as OpenCV implements it, keeps its
strongest responses over the whole frame and then drops those inside the mask; the learned
detectors accept no mask, so the library drops their selected keypoints that fall inside it. For
both, masking can only remove keypoints.

blocks.en:
This section shows why the internal statistics of a robust fit cannot rank pipelines on a dynamic
scene and defines what replaces them: the metrics, the treatment of failures, comparability, the
audit of the reference estimator, and the analysis plan.

对参考估计数字和分析计划的审计。

blocks.en:
Inlier count, inlier ratio, and reprojection error measure the internal consistency of a fit: how
well the correspondences the estimator retained agree with the model fitted to them. On static
scenes they are already known to be weak proxies for accuracy. Barath et al. (2023a) report that the inlier count depends on image resolution, on the inlier threshold and on the
estimator, so that MAGSAC returns far more inliers than its competitors at comparable pose
accuracy, and in the tabulation of Jin et al. (2021a, Table 13) the method with the highest inlier
ratio, R2D2 at 52.9 % 52.9\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} , is outperformed downstream by RootSIFT at 39.6 % 39.6\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} .

blocks.en:
The claim here is stronger, and it follows from the scene rather than from the estimator. A
homography needs four correspondences; a group of objects moving together, such as a stream of
vehicles crossing an intersection, supplies hundreds that are mutually consistent under a single
transform, the one describing their motion. Their coverage ranges from a small fraction of a
high-altitude view to a large share of a low-altitude view over congested lanes, but the estimator
weighs their share of the correspondences, not of the area, so even a small coverage can cast many
votes. Outliers that form a coherent structure of their own bias a robust estimate toward a
compromise between the structures or capture it outright ( Stewart, 1997a ) , and a busy
intersection produces that situation persistently. Wherever the moving group wins, every
internal-consistency check is satisfied by the wrong answer: these statistics are not merely
uninformative but anti-informative . They cannot tell whether it has won; Section 7.3 measures that for the cases studied here.

blocks.en:
The estimator cannot detect this failure on its own. Chum et al. (2005a) detect a scene
dominated by a single plane with a test inside the estimator, because that case is a
degeneracy: the data underconstrain the fundamental matrix, and the deficiency is visible in the
sample. A homography fitted to coherently moving objects is fully determined and over-supported; it
differs from the intended solution only in which part of the scene it describes, which no individual
correspondence encodes. None of the estimators compared here contains a check that could apply:
OpenCV runs DEGENSAC only for the fundamental matrix, and the only tests reaching a homography are
conditions on the minimal sample (no three collinear points, unchanged orientation), which a stream
of vehicles over several lanes satisfies. The information needed, which image content is static, is
external to the estimation problem, so the failure has to be handled by the protocol.

optimized, and never rank a pipeline. What replaces them is the rest of this section: agreement
with an external geometry where one exists ( Section 4.2 ), direct measurement of
background alignment where one does not ( Section 4.3 ), and two measures that make
a moving-object consensus observable, the direction of the error ( Section 4.4 ) and the
share of a moving group’s displacement an estimate follows ( Section 4.5 ).

blocks.en:
The two errors answer different questions. IoU j \IoUop_{j} depends on object size as well as on
registration: a displacement that barely changes the overlap of a bus removes much of a
motorcycle’s overlap. OCE j \OCEop_{j} does not, and it is the quantity a trajectory-extraction pipeline
inherits, since such a pipeline carries each detected box into the reference frame corner by corner
and reads the object’s position off the carried quadrilateral. Because 𝐪 j \mathbf{q}_{j} and 𝐪 ^ j \widehat{\mathbf{q}}_{j} carry the same box, the detector’s localization error cancels, and OCE isolates what registration adds to a trajectory.

blocks.en: 4.5 Measuring capture directly
blocks.zh: 4.5 直接测量捕获量

blocks.en:
The direction of the error is a signature of capture read at the four frame corners, far from the
objects that cause it. Capture can also be measured where it happens. The reference frame’s objects
are found again in frame k k by the procedure the case selection uses ( Section 7.1 ):
each box is compared by appearance with the boxes of similar size in frame k k and accepted only as
a mutual best match. With 𝐲 j \mathbf{y}_{j} the center of the match of reference box j j , its
displacement with the platform’s motion removed by the reference estimator is 𝐦 j = 𝐇 ~ k → ref ⋅ 𝐲 j − 𝐪 ¯ j . \mathbf{m}_{j}\;=\;\widetilde{\mathbf{H}}^{k\rightarrow\mathrm{ref}}\cdot\mathbf{y}_{j}\;-\;\bar{\mathbf{q}}_{j}. (17) A box has moved when ∥ 𝐦 j ∥ \lVert\mathbf{m}_{j}\rVert exceeds a tenth of the median object width:
clear of the apparent motion of a stationary object, which comes from box placement and the
reference estimator’s error, and less than a car covers between consecutive frames at urban speeds.
Moved objects move together with moved object i i when their displacements differ from 𝐦 i \mathbf{m}_{i} by at most a tenth of the median object width or a quarter of ∥ 𝐦 i ∥ \lVert\mathbf{m}_{i}\rVert , whichever is larger: the members of one stream drift apart in
proportion to how far it moved, while opposing or crossing streams never agree. The largest set by
area that moves together with one of its members is the group , G G , the structure a single
wrong homography could fit. The capture fraction of a candidate is the share of the group’s
displacement it follows, λ = median j ∈ G − ( 𝐇 ^ k → ref ⋅ 𝐲 j − 𝐇 ~ k → ref ⋅ 𝐲 j ) ⋅ 𝐦 j ∥ 𝐦 j ∥ 2 . \lambda\;=\;\operatorname*{median}_{j\in G}\;\frac{-\bigl(\widehat{\mathbf{H}}^{k\rightarrow\mathrm{ref}}\cdot\mathbf{y}_{j}-\widetilde{\mathbf{H}}^{k\rightarrow\mathrm{ref}}\cdot\mathbf{y}_{j}\bigr)\cdot\mathbf{m}_{j}}{\lVert\mathbf{m}_{j}\rVert^{2}}. (18) An estimate that agrees with the reference estimator where the group lies has λ = 0 \lambda=0 ; one
that registers the group back onto where it stood in the reference frame, which is what a
homography fitted to the group does, has λ = 1 \lambda=1 ; values between are a compromise fit, pulled
toward the group without registering it. A measurement is captured when λ ≥ 0.1 \lambda\geq 0.1 :
the estimate has moved, where the group lies, by at least a tenth of the group’s displacement. That
lies above what a transform reaches without following the group: the identity, which uses no
features, reaches 0.07 0.07 from the platform’s motion alone, and the reference estimator’s audited
error ( Section 7.2 ) amounts to 0.08 0.08 on the smallest displacement of any group, 5 px 5\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ( Table 7 ). Capture is reported descriptively, with the counts at λ ≥ 0.25 \lambda\geq 0.25 , 0.5 0.5 and 1 1 beside it (files offline_masking_capture.csv and realtime_masking_capture.csv ; the CSV files named in this paper are released with its
data ( Fonod & Geroliminis, 2026b ) ). λ \lambda is defined on pairs whose group holds at
least four objects, and only where the pipeline returned an estimate. Beside it, every measurement
records where the estimate’s inliers lie: the share on annotated objects and the share on objects
that moved. The second undercounts what moves with the objects, since a vehicle’s cast shadow lies
outside its box; λ \lambda does not depend on it. These quantities are diagnostics, like the inlier
statistics they are read against, and never rank a pipeline.

blocks.en: 4.6 Treatment of failures
blocks.zh: 4.6 处理失败

blocks.en:
A registration pipeline can fail outright: too few matches survive filtering, or the robust
estimator returns a degenerate transform. Implementations commonly substitute the identity, the
stabilization library evaluated here among them ( Fonod, 2026g ) , which keeps a campaign running but
hides the failure and biases every metric, because the identity is a plausible answer for a
nearly stationary drone. We therefore admit ⊥ \bot explicitly in Eq. 4 and detect
it from what the estimator returns: an absent inlier count, which every fallback leaves, or a
missing or non-finite matrix. An estimate exactly equal to the identity is not a failure, since
between near-identical frames the estimator returns exactly the identity with thousands of
inliers, and that answer is correct. A finite estimate that drives the third homogeneous
coordinate of Eq. 1 to zero at a corner yields non-finite coordinates, which Eqs. 8 and 9 score as a miss; clamping that division, as some implementations do, would
score a collapsing estimate as merely inaccurate.

the transform the pipeline actually delivered, and so is a pair whose evaluation region is too
small to be read; declining to answer costs exactly what delivering the identity costs.

blocks.zh: 4.7 (中文(简体) ). 将管道置于平等的地位

blocks.en:
A benchmark that compares ten pipelines at one shared set of matcher settings measures the
settings as much as the pipelines. This is the central methodological finding of the benchmarks
reviewed in Section 2 , and we adopt their remedies.

blocks.en:
The ratio-test threshold and the inlier threshold of the robust estimator are both known to be
decisive and to have method-specific optima: the first thresholds a descriptor distance
distribution, a property of the descriptor, and the second a reprojection residual, a property of
keypoint localization accuracy. Efe et al. (2021a) obtain their entire
result by varying the first; Jin et al. (2021a, Sec. 5.3) find its optimum differs per feature.
They are swept jointly rather than sequentially (the inlier threshold alone where the
matcher applies no ratio test: LightGlue and LoFTR), following Barath et al. (2023a) : a looser ratio test admits more outliers, which moves the inlier
threshold that best separates them, so the sequential optimum need not be the joint one. Selection uses Eq. 9 , the quantity the benchmark ranks on, because the threshold maximizing
correspondence-level accuracy is not the one maximizing homography accuracy: a robust estimator
turns a surplus of looser matches into a better fit ( Efe et al., 2021a ) . It is also
conservative: a pipeline keeps the values its preset carries unless the best grid point beats them
on mAA by more than the equivalence margin of 0.01 0.01 ( Section 4.9 ), because where
the optimum is flat the best grid point only moves the values within a set the data cannot tell
apart; Part II starts from Part I’s values in the same way.

blocks.en:
Two further parameters, the downsampling ratio and the feature budget, decide how much work a
pipeline does rather than how it uses it, and the shipped presets do not hand every pipeline the
same amount: the learned models’ ratios are memory bounds. Jin et al. (2021a) report every
method at matched keypoint budgets for this reason, and Barath et al. (2023a) report
accuracy against runtime. We therefore sweep both parameters over every pipeline on the tuning
scenes first, under masking disabled and under OBB masking, and read off a single matched
operating point: the lowest budget at which every pipeline that can reach it is within the
equivalence margin of its own saturation under both masking conditions. Masking removes the highest-contrast
content in the frame, so the saturating budget need not be the same with and without it. If no
budget on the grid meets the criterion, every pipeline runs at the largest one and its shortfall
from saturation is reported. The thresholds are then selected at that operating point, so that
what is tuned is what is run; a pipeline that cannot reach it on the benchmark machine is reported
as such rather than scored at a lower budget. Part II runs at two other points of the same grid, one for offline and one for real-time
registration ( Section 7.1 ); its thresholds are tuned again at each and stated in
pixels of the downsampled frame, so that they keep their size relative to keypoint localization as
the frame shrinks.

blocks.en:
Points are placed in a magnified panel with an exact pixel mapping. In F ref F^{\mathrm{ref}} they are chosen and annotated
manually, on the road surface, clear of every object and of the excluded structure. In each audited
frame every point is first proposed by an image fit that shares nothing with the candidates or the
reference estimator: the point’s 81 × 81 $81$\times$81$ -pixel neighborhood in F ref F^{\mathrm{ref}} , with the objects of both
frames filled with the background mean, is aligned to the frame by an affine enhanced correlation
coefficient fit ( Evangelidis & Psarakis, 2008a ) started from the platform motion of the case selection
( Section 7.1 ), and the proposal stands only if the fit correlates at 0.8 0.8 or
better and the fit back from it returns within half a pixel of the reference point. The annotator
sees each proposal beside the point’s reference neighborhood and accepts it or places the point
manually instead; a dense local fit and a sparse whole-frame homography fail in different ways, so their
agreement is evidence about the estimator, and the review guards against the failures of the fit
itself (a neighboring feature, an occlusion, a point that left the frame). A point without a
standing proposal is placed by hand in a panel that opens near where 𝐇 ~ k → ref \widetilde{\mathbf{H}}^{k\rightarrow\mathrm{ref}} predicts it,
displaced by a hidden offset of a few pixels, so that a click following the panel rather than the
feature can only inflate the residual. On two cases the audited frames were also placed entirely
by hand ( Table 6 ): pooled over both, the unaided clicks lie a median of 0.44 px 0.44\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ( 0.82 px 0.82\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} at the 95 95 th percentile) from the proposals and 0.46 px 0.46\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ( 0.91 px 0.91\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ) from 𝐇 ~ k → ref \widetilde{\mathbf{H}}^{k\rightarrow\mathrm{ref}} ’s predictions, while the proposals lie 0.06 px 0.06\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ( 0.32 px 0.32\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ) from the predictions; on each case the proposals lie closer to the predictions than
either lies to the clicks, which separates the click noise from the estimator’s error. The GCP repeatability is measured by annotating the audited frames of two cases a second time in a
separate session without proposals, the reference frame included; it is the annotation floor,
reported beside Eq. 20 so the two are not conflated. The residual is reported per
temporal-offset bin as well as pooled, because the reference’s error plausibly grows with offset as
shadows move and content turns over; the first of the four audit bins holds offsets of one to three
frames, at which a moving group is still shared with the reference, so that a captured estimate can
be scored against the GCP as well.

The plan below was fixed before the campaigns it governs ran, and the implementation applies it when it
renders a table, so that no number is bolded, ranked, or called a difference by a rule chosen
after the outcome was seen. Like the comparisons of learning methods over several data
sets ( Demšar, 2006a ) , it treats the independent unit, not the measurement, as the
sample, and uses paired nonparametric tests over it.

evidence. In Part II one

are never treated as independent. The nine lie at seven intersections, two of them hovered over in
two sessions; a case is defined by the traffic at its reference frame, which two sessions do not
share, so the case rather than the intersection is the unit.

Every comparison reports the paired difference as an effect size: the Hodges–Lehmann
estimate ( Hodges & Lehmann, 1963a ) of the per-cluster paired differences, with a 95 % 95\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} percentile bootstrap interval ( Davison & Hinkley, 1997a ) obtained by resampling
sites in Part I and cases in Part II, with 10 000 10\,000 draws. Every outcome, mAA
included, is computed per cluster and differenced there, so an interval on mAA is an interval on
the cluster-level paired difference. The test is an exact sign-flip permutation ( Good, 2005a ) of the
per-cluster paired differences: 2 13 2^{13} flips in Part I and 2 9 = 512 2^{9}=512 in Part II, so the
smallest two-sided p p attainable in Part II is 2 / 512 = 0.0039 2/512=0.0039 . After the Holm adjustment
across five outcomes, a masking effect is detectable at the 0.05 0.05 level only if it has the
same sign in all nine cases, or in eight with the dissenting case the smallest in magnitude
( 4 / 512 × 5 = 0.039 4/512\times 5=0.039 ).
The design detects a consistent effect and nothing weaker. The 2 × 2 2\times 2 over moving foreground
and coherence, with two cases per cell, is reported descriptively, without intervals or an
interaction test; the within-case mechanism contrasts test its prediction.

blocks.en: 5 Masking configurations and their annotations
blocks.zh: 5个面具配置及其说明

blocks.en:
Three configurations are evaluated, and the complete benchmark is repeated for each: no masking, HBB masks, and OBB masks. Under the latter two, the annotated boxes of both frames are
rasterized into a binary mask that the feature detector receives, so that no keypoint is detected
on an annotated object; an HBB is rasterized as an axis-aligned rectangle and an OBB as a quadrilateral. Each box is first scaled about its center by 1 + m 1+m with the mask margin m = 0.15 m=$0.15$ , to absorb annotation slack, shadow and motion blur at the object boundary. That
margin belongs to the pipeline and is a hyperparameter of it, distinct from the constant dilation τ \tau of the evaluation region in Eq. 11 , which belongs to the protocol. The HBB is the detector’s and the OBB is fitted to the segmented vehicle, so the two differ in
extent as well as in shape and neither need contain the other; the suppressed-area gap between the
two geometries is reported for every scene set.
blocks.zh:

光栅化为特性探测器接收的二进制口罩,从而不检测出键点

边距属于管道,是管道的一个超参数,不同于Eq. 11中评价区域的常量放大\\tau,它属于协议. 六溴代二苯是探测器,而六溴代二苯则被安装在分叉车辆上,所以两者在以下两个方面有所不同:

blocks.en:
Whether the shape of a mask matters for registration is not obvious in advance, and plausible
mechanisms point both ways. An HBB around a vehicle turned off the image axes also
covers the road beside it, two wedges of asphalt that at an intersection often hold lane markings,
stop lines and curb edges, the static texture the estimator most needs; the wedges grow with the
angle, to about twice the vehicle’s own area for a 40 40 × \times 10 10 box at 45 ° 45\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolDegree} , and in a queue of turning vehicles adjacent HBB merge over the
markings between them. OBB keep that texture. Conversely, what moves with a vehicle is
not confined to its body: its cast shadow, its motion blur and the reflections off its windows
travel with it, lie partly outside a tight OBB , and supply correspondences that agree with
its motion, and the extra area of an HBB covers part of them. Which effect dominates, if
either, is an empirical question, so the box geometry is a controlled axis of both parts, and the
margin sweep of Section 7.5 compares the two geometries at equal suppressed area, so
that a difference can be told apart from the area each removes. OBB are also what the
motion axis of Section 4.4 and the object-level errors of Section 4.2 are read from, whatever the masking.

blocks.en: 5.1 Oriented annotations and the Songdo Vision OBB release
blocks.zh: 5.1 定向说明和Songdo Vision OBB发布

blocks.en:
OBB masks require an oriented annotation for every object in every frame the benchmark
touches, orders of magnitude beyond what can be drawn by hand. They are obtained from the
horizontal annotations by prompting SAM-family segmentation models ( Kirillov et al., 2023a ; Ravi et al., 2025a ) with each box and fitting a minimum-area rotated rectangle ( Freeman & Shapira, 1975a ) to the
resulting mask ( Fonod, 2026e ) ; the procedure and its validation against a human-verified oriented
reference are given in Appendix E . Inside the benchmark the conversion runs over the
vehicle annotations of the scenes and cases under test, the only use on which any number in this
paper depends. Applied to the whole of Songdo Vision ( Fonod et al., 2026a ) at the selected
configuration it yields 274 190 274\,190 OBB over 5419 5419 frames, one per HBB and carrying its class and identifier, released as Songdo Vision
OBB ( Fonod & Geroliminis, 2026c ) with the human-verified reference used
to select and validate the conversion: 4245 4245 OBB over 50 50 frames from six
recordings ( Section E.1 ). None of those 50 50 frames appears in Songdo Vision, as
checked against all 5419 5419 by checksum and by decoded pixels, but they come from the same six
flights. That is a weaker guarantee than the site-level split of Section 4.7 , and the
appropriate one here: the conversion is selected by IoU against a human-verified reference, a quantity
that involves neither the pipelines nor their metrics, so scene overlap cannot tune it toward a
favorable stabilization result; it can only flatter the reported conversion fidelity, which Appendix E therefore states as a tuned-set estimate.

Fig. 2 shows the protocol. Known homographies (translation, rotation about
the frame center, uniform scale, and a small projective term) and a chain of photometric
degradations (brightness, saturation, blur, haze, sensor noise, and JPEG compression) are applied
to static aerial frames, and the pipeline registers the degraded, warped frame back onto the
original, so the ground truth is exact. Trials are paired : the perturbation of a (scene,
trial) does not depend on the pipeline, so every pipeline faces the identical sequence of
perturbations, and every sampled parameter is recorded with its trial. The ranges
( Table 1 ) are those of the published campaign ( Fonod et al., 2025b ) : translation up to 10 % 10\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} of each frame dimension, rotation up to 15 ° 15\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolDegree} , scale within 5 % 5\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} , and a small projective term. This is wider than the deployed hover regime of Section 3 , so that operating limits are measured;
a second configuration at deployment scale (rotation within 2 ° 2\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolDegree} , translation within 2 % 2\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} , scale within 1 % 1\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} , no projective term, the same photometric chain)
is run for the detector axis, and rotation is swept separately beyond the main range.

the estimator axis at two fixed detectors, and the rotation sweep. Trial counts are 30 30 per scene for the tuning-side sweeps, 100 100 for the evaluation
campaigns and 50 50 for the rotation sweep.

blocks.en:
Part I asks which settings of a registration pipeline matter when nothing in the scene moves. The
results follow the settings in the order of their effect: the compute budget, the ratio-test and
inlier thresholds, and the robust estimator; then the ranking they produce at the operating point
and what masking costs. The estimator, deployment and rotation sweeps are given in full in Appendix B .

更高的阈值和稳健的估算值;然后在操作点进行排名
和什么伪装的代价。 附录B全面介绍了估算、部署和轮调情况。

The budget sweep crossed four downsampling ratios ( 0.18 0.18 , 0.30 0.30 , 0.50 0.50 , 1.0 1.0 )
with three feature budgets ( 1000 1000 , 2000 2000 , 8000 8000 ) on the tuning scenes, at the
untuned starting thresholds, since it precedes the tuning ( Fig. 4 ), and it has
the largest effect of the settings in this part. No budget met the criterion of Section 4.7 , so every pipeline runs at the
grid’s ceiling, full resolution with 8000 8000 features, and the pipelines fall into two groups
below it. ORB, XFeat, KeyNet with LightGlue, BRISK and AKAZE are still gaining at the ceiling: from
half to full resolution at 8000 8000 features their unmasked mAA rises by 0.035 0.035 , 0.048 0.048 , 0.023 0.023 , 0.018 0.018 and 0.017 0.017 , so a lower operating point would rank them

largest change is ORB’s gain at a ratio of 0.18 0.18 with 1000 1000 features, which shrinks to 0.017 0.017 at 2000 2000 features and 0.004 0.004 at 8000 8000 ; the largest loss is XFeat’s, 0.034 0.034 at full resolution with 1000 1000 features. Since nothing in these scenes moves, any
such gain is a matter of which features the budget keeps, a point Section 7.5 returns to. At Part II’s real-time point, six of the ten pipelines (ORB, AKAZE, XFeat, SIFT,

blocks.en:
The ratio test and the inlier threshold are the two parameters that earlier benchmarks found
decisive ( Efe et al., 2021a ; Jin et al., 2021a ) , and they are swept jointly for every pipeline
( Section 4.7 ), from untuned starting values: the ratio of 0.9 0.9 that the
stabilization library ships and an inlier threshold of 2 2 to 3 px 3\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} per detector, listed
with the selected values in Table 1 . At the operating point the surfaces are
flat. All 80 80 grid points of SIFT, RootSIFT, ORB, BRISK and AKAZE lie within the equivalence
margin of the best, against 57 57 of XFeat’s; LightGlue applies no ratio test, so its three
pipelines are swept over the threshold alone, and all 8 8 of their points are tied. Tuning
raises mAA over the starting values by 0.0062 0.0062 for XFeat and by at most 0.0011 0.0011 for every
other pipeline. The incumbents are the values each preset carries, and every pipeline keeps them,
since no grid point beats them by more than the margin; the largest gain on offer is 0.0002 0.0002 , for AKAZE at a ratio of 0.8 0.8 . At the kept ratio the inlier threshold moves mAA by at most 0.0002 0.0002 for every
pipeline, so the data do not identify it. The estimator is the reason
( Fig. 1 ): MAGSAC++, the operating estimator, marginalizes over the noise
scale instead of committing to one threshold. Below a ratio of 0.70 0.70 mAA stays flat for SIFT,
RootSIFT, AKAZE and BRISK and falls for ORB and XFeat, so the kept ratios lie on the plateau rather
than at an edge of it.

blocks.en:
The objects in a static scene move with the ground, so masking them removes correct
correspondences or, for a detector that refills its budget, exchanges them for others
( Fig. 3 ), and a small cost is expected. This is the baseline against which the
dynamic results of Section 7.5 are attributed to object motion rather than to
masking as such. OBB masking costs every pipeline less than the equivalence margin. The
largest loss in mAA is 0.0024 0.0024 , for XFeat; for the remaining eight pipelines the change is
below 0.0013 0.0013 in magnitude, and AKAZE, BRISK and KeyNet with LightGlue gain up to 0.0012 0.0012 . HBB masking costs as little: 0.0024 0.0024 for XFeat and at most 0.0008 0.0008 for the other eight pipelines, two of which gain. It scores below OBB masking for every
pipeline but AKAZE, as the larger mask predicts (a median of 3.56 % 3.56\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} of the frame
against 3.32 % 3.32\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} , Table 3 ), but by at most 0.0007 0.0007 , so at these
object densities the extra area an HBB removes costs almost nothing, and a difference
between the two mask shapes in the dynamic benchmark is not explained by the area they remove
alone.

blocks.en:
Figure 5: Part II. Every candidate registers the same frame pairs under each masking mode in turn,
and the reference estimator registers them once, under OBB masks. The reference
estimator supplies pseudo-ground truth and its own error is measured against GCP ; that residual is the equivalence margin of the reference-relative pixel metrics. On the audited frames a homography fitted
to the same points is an independent reference of its own, and the identity transform is scored on
every pair as the unstabilized baseline. The object annotations enter as the feature mask and,
placed by the reference estimator, as the evaluation region and as the object motion that the
capture fraction is read against.

Fig. 5 shows the protocol and Table 3 its constants.
A case is one hover, the recording of one drone over one intersection cut to its stable part,
which lasts two to four minutes ( Fonod et al., 2025b ) , and every sampled frame of it is registered
directly onto one reference frame, as the deployed pipeline does. The reference is a frame the
case selection picks inside the hover rather than its first: traffic at an intersection comes in
phases, and whether a group of vehicles moving together is in view at the reference decides whether
capture can occur at all.

twelve bins one octave wide, 1 1 , 2 2 – 3 3 , 4 4 – 7 7 , 8 8 – 15 15 , and so

that holds that many and every offset of the four shortest, 135 135 pairs per case, each weighing
the same. The spacing follows the mechanism. Capture needs objects present in both frames that

trajectories ( Fonod et al., 2025c ) , over all 20 20 intersections and 4 4 days, about 90 % 90\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} of the vehicles in view at a given instant are still in view 4 s 4\text{\,}\mathrm{s} later, 64 % 64\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} after 16 s 16\text{\,}\mathrm{s} , 45 % 45\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} after 32 s 32\text{\,}\mathrm{s} , 22 % 22\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} after 64 s 64\text{\,}\mathrm{s} and 5 % 5\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} after 120 s 120\text{\,}\mathrm{s} (lower bounds,

within seconds. Evenly spaced offsets would spend most pairs on frames that share no moving group
with the reference and average the effect away; the octaves resolve the shortest offsets, where a

blocks.en:
Every pipeline of Part I is a candidate, so that a ranking that changes between static and dynamic
footage can be observed rather than assumed away, and every candidate runs under all three masking
modes on every pair, so masking is a within-pair factor. SIFT, the reference estimator’s own
detector, is among them, which makes the one pairing that is circular by construction
( Section 4.8 ) explicit. The candidates run in two regimes, both points of Part I’s budget
grid ( Fig. 4 ). The offline regime, for registering a recorded video after
the flight, is half resolution with 2000 2000 features, the operating point of the campaign this
work extends ( Fonod et al., 2025b ) . The real-time regime is the grid’s cheapest point, a
downsampling ratio of 0.18 0.18 with 1000 1000 features, at which six of the ten pipelines
estimate a frame’s transform within one frame interval ( 33.4 ms 33.4\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s} ) at the median on the
benchmark machine. In both, the
inlier threshold is given in pixels of the downsampled frame, so that it keeps its size relative to
keypoint localization. The regimes share the cases, the pairs, the reference estimator and the GCP ; the mask-margin sweep and the repeated runs are made in the offline regime only. Two
further rows are scored on every pair without any pipeline: the identity , which is the
unstabilized frame and the transform a failed pipeline delivers, and the reference estimator

The ratio-test and inlier thresholds are not carried over from Part I, where they were selected
under synthetic warps of static scenes: moving objects change which correspondences are outliers,
and the inlier threshold in particular decides whether matches on a moving group join the
consensus. They are tuned in each regime by Part I’s procedure and selection rule, with Part I’s
values as the incumbents (a joint grid widened to 14 14 ratios from 0.4 0.4 to 0.99 0.99 and 13 13 inlier thresholds from 0.1 0.1 to 16 px 16\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} , selected on mAA, masking disabled),
scored against the reference estimator on five tuning cases that the survey selects, one per cell
and one control, from the intersections of Part I’s tuning scenes, so that no tuning case shares an
intersection with an evaluation case. Offline, SIFT, BRISK and AKAZE move to the strictest corner of

( Tables 1 and 2 ). The selections at

blocks.en:
The hypothesis predicts when capture is severe: where more of the foreground moves, and moves
coherently. Testing that needs footage spanning those conditions, so the nine cases are selected by
design, on the amount and the coherence of the moving foreground as measured from the video. The
candidates come from the hovers of one recording day at the evaluation sites of Part I’s split; the next day in a fixed order is added only if a cell cannot be filled.
Every hover is read at points 30 s 30\text{\,}\mathrm{s} apart, clear of its first and last seconds and with
the full 3600 3600 frames after them, and each point is a candidate reference frame; a hover
supplies at most one case. Each candidate is read the way the benchmark reads it: as pairs of the
candidate reference with one later frame in each of the five shortest offset bins ( 1 1 , 2 2 , 5 5 , 11 11 and 22 22 frames, the bins’ geometric centers), since every benchmark
pair shares the reference and a moving group moves as one only briefly. In each pair the platform’s
motion is removed by an affine enhanced correlation coefficient fit to the
background ( Evangelidis & Psarakis, 2008a ) , with each frame’s objects filled with the background mean,
and every object annotated in the reference frame is sought among the later frame’s detections by
appearance: its patch, resampled along its OBB , is compared by ZNCC , and only a mutual best
match between boxes of similar size is accepted. A reference object is then found where it was,
found displaced (moved by more than a tenth of the median object width), or not found, and the
largest set of displaced objects moving together is the largest structure a single wrong homography
could fit, both as defined for the capture measure ( Section 4.5 ). Averaged over the
offsets, the displaced share of the frame is how many votes the moving foreground can cast, and the
share of it moving as one structure, the coherence , is how many it can cast for one model;
opposing or crossing streams have low coherence however aligned their boxes are. Distances are
measured in object widths, so the procedure does not depend on ground resolution, and nothing is
tracked: six annotated frames per candidate suffice. The design is a 2 × 2 2\times 2 split at the
pool medians ( Table 5 ): a candidate is high moving if its displaced share of
the frame is at or above the median and low moving otherwise, and coherent or mixed by its coherence in the same way. Each cell holds two cases, ranked by their margin
from the split boundaries, with at most one hover per site in a cell; an unfilled cell is reported,
never padded from its neighbor.

motion is absent by construction, gives an independent value of every descriptor for every
candidate ( Table 3 ): the static, moving and coherently moving foreground
correlate with their trajectory values at r = 0.97 r=0.97 , coherence at r = 0.90 r=0.90 and stationarity at r = 0.93 r=0.93 ; the two place 81% of the candidates in the same cell and 97% of the quarter farthest

blocks.en:
A queue at a red light is much foreground with little motion. If masking helps there as much as in a
flowing case, the effect comes from removing texture rather than moving objects, and the proposed mechanism
does not hold. The design therefore includes a stationary control case, a candidate whose reference
foreground mostly stays where it was (the unmoved share of the found foreground in the pool’s top
decile, with at least the pool’s median amount of it). Because one case gives one number, the
control is also defined at the level of the frame pair: the occupancy persistence between the
reference frame’s objects and the current frame’s objects placed in reference coordinates (the
intersection over union of the two footprints) is recorded with every measurement, so moving and
stationary foreground can be compared within one case, under the same background, which is the
comparison the texture confound needs. Table 5 lists the nine cases with the
descriptors they were placed on, Fig. 6 shows each at its reference frame, and file offline_masking_scenes.csv characterizes their frames in the terms of Table 3 .

blocks.en: 7.2 Reference estimator and its audited error
blocks.zh: 7.2 参考估计及其审计错误

blocks.en:
A reference estimator is built from the leading pipelines of Part I under OBB masking ( Table 4 ): AKAZE, RootSIFT, SIFT and BRISK cannot be told apart on mAA,
and SIFT, the most widely used of the four, is taken. It runs at full resolution with a feature
budget of 20 000 20\,000 keypoints, a larger mask margin and a stricter estimator
( Table 2 ), and its ratio-test and inlier thresholds are tuned as every Part I
pipeline is, on the static tuning scenes against their known homographies, at these settings. The
surface is flat, all 70 70 grid points within the equivalence margin of the best, so SIFT’s
values, r = 0.70 r=$0.70$ and θ = 0.5 px \theta=$0.5\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x}$ , are kept, at an mAA of 0.9856 0.9856 ( Table 4 ). Its homographies 𝐇 ~ k → ref \widetilde{\mathbf{H}}^{k\rightarrow\mathrm{ref}} are cached once, so every
candidate is scored against identical geometry. It runs masked because that is the configuration
expected to be most accurate; Section 4.8 states the consequence, which is why the masking
result is read primarily off the GCP and the reference-free measures. Choosing
the reference on Part I’s ranking assumes what the paper questions elsewhere, that static accuracy
transfers to dynamic scenes; it is admissible only because the reference’s accuracy on the dynamic
footage is then measured against independent control points rather than inferred.

the reference, once part of its standing foreground has started to move together, and its captures
lie there. The coherence axis does

blocks.en:
For the average pipeline, OBB masking improves every outcome in most cases: in real time
ZNCC and GOS in eight of nine, the three outcomes against the GCP in seven;
offline the corner error against them in all nine and the others in five or six. No outcome meets
the rule of Section 4.9 in either regime, and the primary contrast is not claimed. HBB masks against none read the same way, and OBB against HBB masks differ on no
outcome in either regime
( Tables 12 and 13 ). Four of the nine cases
never present a moving group, so an average over cases and pipelines dilutes an effect confined to
a few pairs of a few cases and of one pipeline.

blocks.en:
Masking can help in two ways. It removes the correspondences on the
objects, from which a captured fit is built, and, for a detector that applies the mask before it
caps its keypoints ( Section 3.2 ), it hands the removed share of the budget to the ground
whether or not the objects moved. The first predicts a benefit concentrated on pairs with a moving
group, a captured share that falls under masking, and an error that loses its alignment with the
motion. The second predicts a benefit for the detectors that refill their budget, largest at small
budgets, that appears in the stationary control and on Part I’s static scenes as well. Both act on
ORB, and the two protocols give evidence of each. The budget effect is real: on Part I’s static scenes OBB masking raises ORB’s mAA by 0.065 0.065 at the real-time point ( Section 6.2 ),
where Part II’s real-time ORB rises from 0.5835 0.5835 to 0.6785 0.6785 . The captured pairs cannot
account for most of that rise. A pair weighs 1 / 135 1/135 of its case and the cases weigh equally, so the 28 28 captured pairs can move ORB’s mAA by at most 28 / ( 9 × 135 ) = 0.023 28/(9\times 135)=0.023 , and ORB gains in eight of
the nine cases although only five ever hold a moving group ( Table 13 );
the rest of the rise is of the size of the budget effect on static scenes. A budget effect cannot
make an estimate follow a group, however, and the capture fraction finds that only without masking.
The strata agree: in real time the reference-free benefit of the
average pipeline is largest in the high-moving mixed cell, which holds S2, and near zero in the
low-moving cells and the stationary control (file realtime_masking_benefit_strata.csv ). The
mechanism contrasts point the same way for ORB in real time, with a positive coverage correlation,
a positive persistence gap and a positive alignment contrast, each with an interval above zero and
none meeting the rule after Holm’s adjustment. For the average pipeline only the real-time
persistence gap in ZNCC has an interval above zero, and offline no contrast points toward capture
(files offline_masking_mechanism.csv and realtime_masking_mechanism.csv ). In real time the benefit of
the average pipeline is positive in every offset bin and both persistence halves, larger for pairs
whose foreground moved, and by cell largest in the high-moving cells; offline it is smaller by an
order of magnitude and mixed between 16 16 and 127 127 frames
(files offline_masking_benefit_strata.csv and realtime_masking_benefit_strata.csv ). With two cases per
cell the design reads them descriptively; the within-case contrasts, which match coverage and weigh
every case equally, are the test.

blocks.en: 8.1 Interpretation of the capture measurement
blocks.zh: 8.1 捕获量度的解释

blocks.en:
Consensus capture is the failure the dynamic protocol was built to measure. In these nine cases it
occurs without masking: for ORB at both budgets, in real time in every case that presents a
coherently moving group, and by a pixel or two, at the limit of what the GCP resolve, for BRISK, SIFT and RootSIFT at the real-time budget. Under masking it occurs nowhere. This
bears on the pipeline with which Fonod et al. (2025b) extracted the
Songdo Traffic trajectories ( Fonod et al., 2025c ) , ORB at the offline budget under HBB masks: unmasked, it is captured on 6 6 pairs, masked on none, which supports masking at
detection for trajectory extraction. Three properties make this a measurement rather than an anecdote. The
instruments resolve it: a complete capture misaligns the fit where the moving group lies by a
sizable fraction of an object width, far above the audited error of the reference and the
repeatability of the GCP , and a partial capture still raises the capture
fraction and the motion alignment. The cases were chosen to contain it: selected from the video alone,
at reference points spread over every hover of a recording day, they span the amount and
coherence of moving foreground that pool offers. And the tests were fixed before the outcome: the
primary and mechanism contrasts were specified in advance and are reported whatever their result. Capture
itself is counted descriptively, at a threshold above what the identity transform reaches, with the
counts at stricter thresholds beside it. Of the two descriptors the cases were
selected on, the moving share orders where capture occurs and coherence does not: the case with
most captures lies in a mixed cell, because the survey averages coherence over its offsets while a
capture needs one coherent group at one offset ( Section 7.3 ).

blocks.en: 8.2 Joint reading of the two protocols
blocks.zh: 8.2 联合阅读两项议定书

blocks.en:
Part I ranks pipelines against exact truth on static scenes and shows which of their settings
matter there: the compute budget, by a wide margin, then the estimator’s threshold for estimators
that commit to one, while the matcher thresholds have little effect at the operating point and
masking costs almost nothing. Part II asks whether that ranking survives footage in which part of
the frame moves. Capture predicts a specific pattern: a pipeline falls without masking, recovers
under masking, and has its error along the motion while unmasked, with a capture fraction near one on the
pairs that carry a moving group. The data show that pattern for ORB at the real-time budget: its
unmasked estimates follow the group with a capture fraction up to 0.96 0.96 within the survey’s
offsets ( Fig. 1 ), and its error along the motion rises; the alignment rises little,
since the captures are a few percent of the pairs. Its fall from 0.6785 0.6785 masked to 0.5835 0.5835 unmasked is mostly not on the captured pairs, which bound their share of it at 0.023 0.023 ,
and the rest is of the size of the budget effect, which masking has on static scenes as well
( Section 7.5 ). For the other pipelines the static ranking carries over: SIFT, RootSIFT and AKAZE
lead Part II in both regimes, masked or not. The static masking cost is the control that makes
that reading possible: in Part I the annotated objects satisfy the same homography as the
background, so suppressing them cannot improve the consensus, only change which correspondences the
budget keeps.

blocks.en: 8.3 Practical guidance
blocks.zh: 8.3 实际指导

blocks.en:
No single pipeline is called best. The leading tie set on mAA is AKAZE, RootSIFT, SIFT and BRISK
under the main Part I configuration and grows to six pipelines at deployment-scale perturbation;
beyond 30 ° 30\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolDegree} of rotation the upright learned models drop out ( Fig. 2 ).
In Part II the tie set against the reference is SIFT, RootSIFT and AKAZE under every masking mode
in both regimes; against the GCP every configuration ties at the median in both,
and at the 90 90 th percentile all but ORB in real time ( Fig. 11 ). Offline,
masking offers little a practitioner could act on: every configuration lies within the repeatability
of the GCP , and the masking benefits are tenths of a pixel or less. In real time
it makes ORB usable, at a cost on static scenes of less than 0.005 0.005 mAA. For a real-time pipeline the choice is open: masked ORB
registers in 12 12 to 13 ms 13\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s} at a median error of 1.17 1.17 to 1.19 px 1.19\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} against the GCP , and SIFT, RootSIFT and AKAZE, masked or not, in 18 18 to 22 ms 22\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s} at 0.51 0.51 to 0.57 px 0.57\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} ; all fit one frame interval at the median, and for the latter three masking changes
background alignment by less than 0.001 0.001 in either direction, which no contrast resolves
( Tables 9 , 11 and 13 ). Compute excludes some pipelines on
its own: LoFTR cannot run at Part I’s full resolution on the benchmark GPU, and four of the ten
(BRISK, LoFTR, and DeDoDe and KeyNet with LightGlue) need more than one frame interval at the
real-time point. HBB and OBB do not differ measurably for registration at
these densities and orientations, in the masking contrasts or in the margin sweep; a road grid oblique to
the image, larger vehicles at a lower altitude or long turning queues would give the geometry more
room to matter, and the protocol measures it there unchanged. OBB remain useful elsewhere, in the
motion axis of Section 4.4 and in object-level errors that respect an object’s extent.
SIFT and the learned detectors apply the mask after selecting their keypoints in the library
evaluated here ( Section 3.2 ), so for them masking can only remove keypoints; selecting
after the mask is a change to the library, which the protocol would measure unchanged.

blocks.en: 8.4 Limitations
blocks.zh: 8.4 限制

blocks.en:
The cases come from one recording day at one altitude band, and their moving foreground at the
reference covers at most 1.94 1.94 % of the frame, so what is found about capture holds for that
range. Each case is registered onto one reference frame, chosen to span the conditions capture
depends on; how often capture occurs over all the frames a deployed pipeline might register onto is
a different quantity, which the design does not estimate. Part II has nine independent units at seven intersections: a
masking effect is detectable only if it has the same sign in all of them, or in eight with the
dissenting case the smallest, and the 2 × 2 2\times 2 with two cases per cell is descriptive. Taking
the intersection as the unit leaves every claim unchanged, but the per-pipeline benefits that meet
the rule fall short of it, since seven units cannot pass Holm’s adjustment over ten pipelines, and
ORB’s real-time coverage correlation loses its interval above zero. Cases
with a larger moving share, from lower altitudes or congested approaches, and
more sites and sessions are the most informative extension; the selection procedure is automated
so that they can be added without revisiting the design.

different registration model.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en:
Coherently moving objects can capture the geometric consensus of a robust estimator, and the
statistics that describe a fit’s self-consistency would then describe the wrong fit. This paper
turns that possibility into a measurement for the complete registration pipeline used in
reference-frame stabilization of hovering-drone video. A static protocol under exact ground truth
establishes what each pipeline can do. A dynamic protocol on nine intersection cases, each
registered onto a reference frame selected from the video alone, measures what the same pipelines
do when part of the frame moves, at an offline and a real-time budget, with a ground-control-point
audit that measures the error of the pseudo-ground-truth reference and scores every candidate
independently of it.

Two conventions are worth stating, because a reader comparing against published numbers for the
same detectors will otherwise be comparing different quantities. First, the inlier threshold is
expressed in pixels of the full-resolution reference frame whatever the processed
resolution, which is the convention of the stabilization library: the pipelines estimate current → \to reference, so the reprojection residual is evaluated there, and a threshold quoted in the
other frame differs by the scale factor of the transform. Part I’s ranking campaigns and

frame coincide, and Part I’s budget sweep keeps the library’s convention. Part II’s two regimes
state the threshold in pixels of the downsampled frame instead, so that Part I’s values, from which
their tuning starts, keep their size relative to keypoint localization; 4 px 4\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} is 8 px 8\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} at
full resolution in the offline regime and about 22 px 22\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x} in the real-time one. Because every threshold is tuned at the operating
point it is run at, no reported number depends on a rescaling between resolutions. Second, all reported
values are for the implementations and versions recorded in each result manifest; as Barath et al. (2023a) document, the same nominal algorithm can differ measurably between

blocks.en:
Jin et al. (2021a) run each evaluation three times and average the results to reduce the
randomness in them, which they found negligible. We report single runs instead, having measured
how random the estimators used here are. On the OpenCV build recorded in the manifests, homography
estimation does not change its output across different global random seeds, at outlier
fractions up to 75 % 75\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} , and does not advance the global random stream either; each
estimator seeds an internal generator from a fixed constant.
Every method is additionally bit-identical across repeated calls on identical input, with one
exception: the parallel LO-RANSAC variant returns one of a small set of matrices depending on
thread scheduling, a race that no seed removes. Its spread is at most 1.5 × 10 − 3 1.5\times 10^{-3} px of corner transfer on a 3840 × 2160 3840\times 2160 frame, more than two orders
of magnitude below the smallest audited resolution floor of Table 6 and therefore
not a limitation on any claim made here. For the OpenCV estimators, results are consequently
reproducible exactly rather than in distribution. The learned detectors and matchers run under
a tensor library whose kernel selection on a GPU is not guaranteed to be bit-exact, so that
argument does not extend to them, and the learned pipelines of Part II’s offline regime were
repeated three times on one case instead.
The repeats agree: every learned pipeline under every masking mode returned the same estimate
on all 135 135 pairs in all three repeats, and no pair changed between success and failure
(released file offline_repeats_repeat_spread.csv ).

blocks.en:
Each HBB , its sides moved outward by a scale factor s s of its width and height (each
dimension grows by 2 ​ s 2s ), prompts one or more SAM-family
models ( Kirillov et al., 2023a ; Ravi et al., 2025a ) , and an ensemble’s masks are combined by majority vote.
The mask is cropped to the scaled prompt and refined by a signed morphological
step ( Soille, 2004a ) , its square kernel a set fraction of the shorter side of the
largest contour’s bounding rectangle: a positive kernel opens it, removing a
thin protrusion such as an overhead sign enclosed by the box, and a negative kernel closes it,
rejoining a body split by glare or an occluder. A minimum-area rotated
rectangle ( Freeman & Shapira, 1975a ) is fitted to the largest contour together with any piece
holding at least a set fraction of its area. The OBB keeps the class of its HBB ;
where no valid mask is found, the HBB is emitted unchanged, the fallback whose
consequence is stated in Section 5 .

blocks.en:
The reference is 4245 4245 OBB over 50 50 frames from six recordings. A detector
supplied the HBB ; one annotator went over every frame and redrew as OBB the 1345 1345 vehicles not square to the image, leaving the other 2900 2900 on their detected geometry,
and the set was restricted to the four vehicle classes, rectified to true rectangles, and
reconciled one-to-one with the HBB that prompt the conversion, each the exact axis-aligned
envelope of its OBB . The unrevised boxes are about 5.8 % 5.8\text{\,}\mathrm{\%} wider across the
vehicle than hand-drawn ones, so on the axis-aligned majority mean IoU mixes reference slack with
conversion error. An independent
DOTA-pretrained oriented detector ( YOLO11x-OBB ( Jocher & Qiu, 2024a ) , run tiled and
scored class-agnostically), which shares neither architecture nor training data with the conversion,
places the axes of these vehicles within a median 0.82 ° 0.82\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolDegree} of the reference boxes, the scale
against which the conversion’s orientation error is read.
